title: From Sketch to Insight: Drawing and Property Calculation with Marvin and Chemically Intelligent Toolkits
summary: Go from a sketched molecule to a full design set. See Marvin and chemically intelligent toolkits predict logP, logD, pKa and CNS properties live on Nov 4.

ShareShareShare


**Sessions:** November 4, 2026. Three live sessions, each starting at 1:00 PM local time:


1:00 PM JST (Japan)


1:00 PM CET (Central Europe)


1:00 PM ET (US East Coast)


- [Discovery](https://www.certara.com/resource-solution/discovery/)


**Products:**[Marvin](https://www.certara.com/marvin/) ,[Toolkits](https://www.certara.com/discovery-toolkit/)


## Summary


Every cheminformatics workflow starts with a structure and ends with a decision. But what happens when you need to go from sketching a single molecule to enriching an entire compound library? Chemaxon’s Marvin and Chemistry Toolkit cover both ends of that journey!


In this session, Certara’s Zsolt Skribanek will walk through a real workflow, live. Starting with a few early leads drawn in Marvin and on-the-fly predictions of logP, logD, pKa and CNS properties, you will then see the same calculations scaled to a whole design set of structures with chemically intelligent toolkits. Side-by-side examples show exactly when to use each, and how to combine them.


## What you’ll learn


- **Draw and calculate, interactively.** Create and curate structures quickly in Marvin, abstract the common scaffold, and generate a design set by using Markush enumeration capabilities, and get property predictions as you draw, with publication-ready visuals.
- **Scale from one molecule to thousands.** See how chemically intelligent toolkits power high-throughput batch calculation, data enrichment, and automated pipelines.
- **Pick the right tool for the job.** Compare Marvin’s interactive experience with the scriptable, dataset-scale power of chemically intelligent toolkits, and leave knowing when to use one, the other, or both.


## Register now


## Who should attend


- Chemists who draw and evaluate structures in their daily work
- Cheminformaticians building batch calculation and data enrichment workflows
- Research teams relying on molecular property calculation across projects
- Marvin and Chemaxon users exploring desktop and batch options


## Speaker:


[Zsolt Skribanek](https://www.certara.com/teams/zsolt-skribanek/) Senior Application Scientist, Certara


Zsolt Skribanek holds a degree in chemistry and a Ph.D. in organic chemistry from Eötvös Loránd University in Budapest. During his doctoral studies, he worked as a research scientist in the Spectroscopic Research Division of Hungary’s largest pharmaceutical company, specializing in mass spectrometry and Raman spectroscopy.


With over 20 years of experience in cheminformatics, Zsolt joined Chemaxon – acquired by Certara in 2025 – in 2016. As a Senior Application Scientist, he supports customers and distributors across the Asia-Pacific region.
